    How this works
    

      
Each entry holds tickets — one, unless you write ×3, x3 or
        *3 after it for three. A pick draws one ticket from all the tickets still in the hat,
        using crypto.getRandomValues and throwing away any draw that would favour the first
        entries, so an entry with three tickets is exactly three times as likely as one with a single
        ticket, and nothing else tilts it. The same name written on two lines counts as two entries; the
        page points that out, because it is usually a pasting accident rather than a decision.

      
Picking several at once draws them one after another without putting any back, so the same entry
        never appears twice in one pick, and the order they come out is the order printed — first place,
        second place. Take winners out keeps them out for the next press as well, which is
        right for a raffle with several prizes or for going round a room; untick it and every press draws
        from the full list again. Put everyone back refills the hat without touching the
        list.

      
The list is read afresh whenever you edit it, and the record of who has been picked lives in this
        tab only: close it and it is gone. Nothing you paste is sent or stored; the Dark and language buttons keep their
        own settings in this browser's local storage. Up to 5,000 entries, and up to 1,000 tickets each.
